title: Pomiches Creek (East Moriches)
summary: Pomiches is an East Moriches creek placename remembered as the western boundary of Watchogue Neck and interpreted as a crossing or crossway.
map_geometry_source: Approximate East Moriches creek/valley point near Montauk Highway, used as a general proxy for Pomiches Creek at the west side of Watchogue Neck; exact historic creek head, marsh, and path crossing need local map review.
introduction_content: Pomiches names a creek at East Moriches, associated with Watchogue Neck and the creek-and-path landscape of Unkechaug homelands on the south shore.
history_content: Pomiches belongs to the East Moriches boundary landscape with Watchogue Neck and Mattuck Brook. Sale, village, swamp, and spelling details appear in the historic moments below.
translation_content:
Related forms include Pameeches, Pamachees Pond, and Permichees Swamp. The name is interpreted as a crossing, something coming from the side, or a crossway, possibly referring to a creek and path crossing.

Why Place Names Matter

“Place names conserve the cultural memory of communities and peoples as well as the memory of natural processes and events.”

— Přemysl Mácha, Wherein lies the heritage value of place names? (2023), PDF page 20
whereintheworld_content: Approximate/general point in East Moriches near the historic creek/valley landscape west of Watchogue Neck. This marker is not an exact creek-head, marsh, path-crossing, or village coordinate.
